paper_id: Effective Deep Memory Networks for Distant Supervised Relation Extraction
title: Effective Deep Memory Networks for Distant Supervised Relation Extraction
motivation: Distant supervision generates noisy multi-instance multi-label data; existing neural models ignore context word importance and inter-relation dependencies
problem_framing: Multi-instance multi-label relation extraction with noisy labels from knowledge base alignment
key_insight: Use two-level attention memory networks: word-level to weight context words by entity-pair relevance, relation-level to model inter-relation dependencies and reduce noise
method_signature: Two-layer memory networks: word-level (6-hop) attention for sentence representation, relation-level (2-layer) attention for bag-of-instances multi-label classification
evaluation_criteria: Precision-recall curve and P@N (Top-100/200/500) on NYT10 distant supervision dataset
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: When hop count exceeds 6, results degrade; gradient vanishing problem as memory network goes deeper
evidence_for_taste: neural-based methods are extremely strong performer
DMN provides superior performance to all other methods
when the number of hops exceeds 6, the experimental results become worse
The reason might lie in the gradient vanishing problem
thinking_moves: Identifies two unmodeled phenomena: context word importance and inter-relation dependencies
Selects memory networks as the architectural vehicle because they enable explicit read/write of importance weights
Ablates each memory component separately to isolate their contributions
Finds optimal hop depth empirically; treats saturation as a limitation rather than forcing deeper model
